record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Fix ell in {1, ..., m}. An ell-Volterra QSO is a quadratic stochastic operator whose heredity coefficients are Volterra-like for offspring types 1 through ell, while for offspring types ell+1 through m at least one genuinely non-Volterra heredity coefficient is positive. For a given ell-Volterra QSO, determine the full set of its periodic trajectories, beyond the vertex cycles whose existence is known for some families.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 2$ and let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m:\ x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the $(m-1)$-dimensional standard simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the heredity coefficients $p_{ij,k}$ satisfy $p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}\ge 0$ for all $i,j,k$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$. The QSO is called Volterra if $p_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$.

Fix $\ell\in\{1,\dots,m\}$. A QSO $V$ is called an $\ell$-Volterra QSO if:
(i) for every $k\in\{1,\dots,\ell\}$ one has $p_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$ (the Volterra condition holds for offspring types $1,\dots,\ell$);
(ii) for each $k\in\{\ell+1,\dots,m\}$ there exists at least one pair $(i,j)$ with $k\notin\{i,j\}$ and $p_{ij,k}>0$ (genuinely non-Volterra behavior for offspring types $\ell+1,\dots,m$).

For $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$, the trajectory of $V$ starting from $x^{(0)}$ is the sequence $x^{(n)}=V^n(x^{(0)})$, $n\ge 0$. A point $x\in S^{m-1}$ is periodic with period $p\ge 1$ if $V^p(x)=x$ and $V^q(x)\ne x$ for $1\le q<p$.

It is known that for every subset $I_s=\{e_{i_1},\dots,e_{i_s}\}\subset\{e_{\ell+1},\dots,e_m\}$ of vertices of $S^{m-1}$ (with $1\le s\le m-\ell$), there exists a family of $\ell$-Volterra QSOs for which $I_s$ forms an $s$-cycle of vertices.

Problem: For a given $\ell$-Volterra QSO $V$ on $S^{m-1}$, determine the set of all its periodic trajectories in $S^{m-1}$ (going beyond the vertex cycles described above).
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of describing the complete set of periodic trajectories for an arbitrary ℓ-Volterra QSO appears to remain open. Partial results exist: vertex cycles are known to exist for prescribed subsets of vertices, and complete classifications of fixed and periodic points have been obtained in low-dimensional cases (m=2,3) and for certain superpositions, but no general description across all m and ℓ has been established.

status_evidence.title: On Dynamics of ℓ-Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the structure of ℓ-Volterra operators and describes several fixed and periodic points; trajectory behavior is described only for m=2 and m=3.
status_evidence.claim: Only low-dimensional cases are fully described; general periodic structure remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Describes periodic and fixed points for a specific superposition class and shows trajectories converge to periodic ones or diverge.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work resolves periodic-point sets only for specific subclasses, not the general ℓ-Volterra case.
